PullRequest.Title: sessions: show automation sessions in the Sessions list on reply or on request
PullRequest.Body:

## What

Automation run sessions are listed only in Automations. This lets a user also bring one into the Sessions list:

- **On request:** *Show in Sessions List* in a run's context menu in Automations. *Hide from Sessions List* (in both Automations and the Sessions list) lists it only in Automations again.
- **Automatically:** `sessions.list.showAutomationSessions` (experimental, experiment-enabled) controls when automation sessions also appear in the Sessions list: `always`, `afterReply` (default — once the user sends a message in the session), or `never`.
- **Explicit choices win:** an explicit Hide is persisted, so neither later messages nor the `always` setting bring the session back, across reloads and restarts. *Show in Sessions List* clears it and lists the session even when the setting is `never`.
- **Automations entry indicator:** the unread / in-progress / needs-input indicator on the Automations entry ignores runs whose session is in the Sessions list, so that state appears only on the session's own row. Runs whose session hasn't loaded yet still count.

## How

- `ISessionsListModelService` owns the listing rule and state (`isSessionListed`, `showAutomationSessions`, `showRepliedAutomationSession`, `hideAutomationSessions`): explicit shown/hidden sets in profile-scoped storage keyed by session ID, plus the setting. Changing the setting fires list changes for affected sessions. It's client-side, so it works for every provider's automation runs, survives temporary provider-catalog eviction, and is cleared only on deletion.
- `AutomationSessionsListingContribution` listens to `IChatService.onDidAcceptRequest`, which already excludes system-initiated and hidden requests. Automation runs are dispatched remotely (agent host / GitHub), so a run's own prompt never lists it.
- The Sessions list, its filter options (creating applications), agent tools, and the Automations status indicator all use the same `isSessionListed` rule instead of a hard-coded `!isAutomation`.
- Accessibility help for the Agents window chat and the Automations view describes the actions and setting; actions announce their result.
- `SESSIONS_LIST.md` / `AUTOMATIONS.md` updated for the new list-owned state.

## How to test

1. Open an automation run from Automations and send a message → it appears in the Sessions list (and stays in Automations).
2. In the Sessions list, *Hide from Sessions List* → it's removed; send another message → it stays hidden. Reload the window → still hidden.
3. In Automations, *Show in Sessions List* → it reappears.
4. With an unread or running automation session, the Automations entry shows the indicator; after *Show in Sessions List*, the indicator moves to the session row.
5. Set `sessions.list.showAutomationSessions` to `never` → replying no longer lists the session; set it to `always` → every automation session you haven't hidden appears.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"` — passed (8809 passing)
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>` — passed
- Manually launched Code OSS (Agents window) for testing; end-to-end UI flow not automated.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The new AfterRestored contribution subscribes to the global accepted-request event, which fires synchronously for every non-system, visible user request. The called implementation constructs a merged array of every provider's sessions and scans each session's chats until a match, before the new code can reject ordinary non-automation sessions.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU, a newly allocated merged session array, chat-array traversals, and URI equality comparisons
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The added work is O(S+C) per accepted request, where S is every loaded session across providers and C is the chats inspected before the owner is found; `_getMergedSessions()` allocates all S entries even when the active session matches early, so total cost grows with catalog size times message frequency.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased synchronous message-submit latency and UI-thread CPU/GC pressure; queued requests are also delayed before `processPendingRequests` starts
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this contribution, accepting a request did not perform this session-catalog ownership lookup for automation-listing purposes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every accepted request now calls `getSessionForChatResource` before checking whether the owner is an automation session or whether the setting is `afterReply`, so regular sessions and disabled/non-applicable modes pay the full catalog scan too.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The newly added listener at lines 34-35 invokes `sessionsManagementService.getSessionForChatResource(chatSessionResource)` for the global request event; there was no automation-listing listener or per-send catalog scan before this PR.
Findings.Title: Avoid scanning the full session catalog on every chat send
Findings.Impact: Sending any ordinary chat message now synchronously rebuilds and scans the complete provider session catalog. Users with long session histories or many nested chats pay this cost on every message even though almost all such requests cannot change automation listing state.
Findings.Evidence: `ChatService.notifyAccepted` synchronously fires `onDidAcceptRequest` for every accepted non-system, visible submission; in the queued path it does so before `processPendingRequests`. `SessionsManagementService.getSessionForChatResource` first calls `_getMergedSessions()` (which concatenates every provider catalog), then loops each session and linearly searches `session.chats` plus `mainChat`. The new listener performs that call before `session?.isAutomation` and before reading `SESSIONS_LIST_SHOW_AUTOMATION_SESSIONS_SETTING`.
Findings.Recommendation: Do not resolve ownership through a full catalog scan for every global request. At minimum gate on `AfterReply` before lookup; then route automation replies through an automation/session-specific signal or add/reuse an authoritative resource-to-session index in the management service so ordinary sends and repeated replies are O(1) rather than rebuilding and scanning the catalog.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed renderer now maps the complete aggregate run history and linearly searches the complete loaded-session catalog for every run before any priority check. The cloud store fetches up to 50 runs per automation and republishes history every 15 seconds while a run is active, so the multiplicity and repeated UI-path execution are directly established; only the exact frame-time cost depends on user history size.
Findings.PerformanceResource: URI equality checks, temporary run/status objects, and filtered arrays on the renderer's synchronous observable derivation
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each history publication now performs O(R*S) session matching before checking run priority, where R is the aggregate retained run count (up to 50 per cloud automation) and S is the full loaded session catalog; this repeats every 15 seconds while any cloud run is active.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: periodic CPU and allocation spikes on the UI thread, causing slower rendering and possible interaction jank for users with substantial automation history and session catalogs
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The previous derivation checked statuses in priority order with short-circuiting: it resolved sessions only for running runs while checking NeedsInput, returned immediately when any pending/running run existed, and inspected completed history only when no active run existed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added map eagerly resolves a session with a full `automationSessions.find(...)` for every historical run and allocates an intermediate object for every run before the later NeedsInput/InProgress checks can return.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The PR adds `runs.read(reader).map(...)` and the per-run `automationSessions.find(...)` at lines 2426-2428 ahead of all status checks, replacing the deleted status-specific `some(...)` passes that returned on NeedsInput or any pending/running run before examining completed history.
Findings.Title: Preserve status short-circuiting before resolving historical runs
Findings.Impact: While an automation is pending or running, the cloud provider refreshes history every 15 seconds. Each refresh can now scan the entire loaded session catalog once per retained run before rendering the Automations indicator, even though an early active run already determines the indicator; large histories can produce recurring UI-thread CPU/GC spikes.
Findings.Evidence: `automationService.runs` is documented as all runs across all automations. `GitHubCloudAutomationStore.refreshHistory` requests `per_page: 50` for every automation and publishes the flattened history, while `CloudAutomationStore` schedules another refresh every 15 seconds when any run is pending/running. `automationSessions` is assigned `this.sessions`, the full session catalog. The added line therefore performs one linear URI search per aggregate run before the active-status checks; the deleted implementation deferred completed-run matching until after active checks.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the priority checks lazy, or build one resource-keyed session map in O(S) and scan runs without intermediate arrays. In particular, determine NeedsInput/InProgress before resolving completed historical runs, while applying `isSessionListed` only to candidates whose status can affect the current result.

Scenarios.Scenario: Chat submission, automation listing, and automation-status refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Accepted chat events synchronously run the new owner lookup; queued sends wait for it. Listing changes synchronously update storage and the visible list. Separately, cloud history publication synchronously recomputes the Automations indicator.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Per-send lookup scales with all sessions and chats. Indicator computation scales with aggregate runs times loaded sessions; cloud history can contain 50 runs per automation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Request listeners and renderer computation are serial on the UI thread. Listing updates are batched. Existing cloud history requests use a concurrency limit of four.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Owner lookup is repeated without an index. Listing sets are cached and skip no-op writes. Cloud history is cached but refreshed every 15 seconds while a run is active.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High; event, storage, polling, and renderer call paths were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact latency depends on catalog size, while the changed synchronous mechanisms and scaling are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Two reportable regressions: full-catalog work on every send and eager quadratic matching on active-history refresh.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all changed files and submitted two performance findings.
